mainTopic: Dislocated thighs in birds, testing for טרפה, and the twelve-month sign of a טרפה
overview: The amud asks whether a bird whose thigh bone slipped out of its socket (שמוטת ירך) is kosher. רב הונא reports in the name of רב that it is כשרה, and רב explicitly separates a dislocated thigh (כשרה) from a cut one (פסולה). But רבי זירא reports in the name of רב and רבי יוחנן that it is a טרפה, while רבי permitted such a hen in a real case. The גמרא rules against the permissive views. It shows this through רבי יהושע בן לוי, who calls a dislocated bird thigh a 'widespread הלכה' of טרפה and explains that animals which seem to survive only lived within twelve months. Next comes the story of רבי שמעון בן חלפתא, who tested rulings. His hen regrew its lost down, against רבי יהודה, and his ant experiment, testing a פסוק in משלי, turns out not to prove anything. רב הונא then sets twelve months as the sign of a טרפה, and the גמרא shows this follows the תנא רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The amud ends with the ruling that a טרפה can give birth and improve, and אמימר begins a statement about eggs of a טרפה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא rules that a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא reports that רב הונא told him a bird with a dislocated thigh is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We had a chance to speak before רב הונא and we asked him. He told us: a bird whose thigh is dislocated is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא tells over a ruling he heard straight from רב הונא: a dislocated thigh does not make a bird a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the starting position for the whole discussion. 'Dislocated' means the bone slipped out of its socket but was not cut off. The rest of the passage tests whether this really matches what רב held.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening to speak, a chance to ask
A thigh bone that slipped out of its socket (dislocated)

phrases.english: We had an opportunity to speak
before Rav Huna, and we asked him,
and he said to us:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לַן פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה (רב הונא).

steps.title: Why is Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba checking the bird's thigh sinews?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא sees רבי ירמיה בר אבא inspecting birds at the צומת הגידין and challenges him with רב הונא's ruling in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: I also found רבי ירמיה בר אבא sitting and checking birds at the meeting point of the sinews. I challenged him: Don't you hold like רב הונא, who said in the name of רב that a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is surprised that someone is checking the thigh area of birds, since רב said a dislocated thigh does not make a bird a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a bird stays kosher even when its thigh slips out of place, it seems pointless to inspect that area. So the checking looks like it goes against רב's ruling. Notice that here רב הונא's ruling is quoted in the name of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The point where the sinews of the thigh meet

phrases.aramaic: וְאַשְׁכַּחְתֵּיהּ נָמֵי לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: And I also found Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba
sitting and checking at the convergence of the sinews,
phrases.notes: He was checking birds there. The גמרא leaves that word out.

phrases.english: and I challenged him:
Doesn't the master hold

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that which Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling from step 1 to question a practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's practice of checking birds at the צומת הגידין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a dislocated thigh is kosher, there seems to be no reason to inspect the thigh sinews.

steps.title: The משנה about cut legs, which רב applied to birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers from a משנה: an animal whose legs were cut above the joint, or whose צומת הגידין was removed, is פסולה. רב said the same is true of birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I know the משנה. An animal whose legs were cut off: below the knee joint it is kosher, above the knee joint it is unfit. The same applies if the meeting point of the sinews was removed. And רב said about this: the same is true for a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה explains his checking. He relies on a משנה and on רב's comment that its rule also applies to birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damage above the joint, or to the צומת הגידין, makes an animal a טרפה. רב extended this to birds, so that area of a bird has to be checked. Now we have two statements in the name of רב that seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: The knee joint of the leg
And the same applies to a bird

phrases.english: He said to me: I know a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in חולין 76a.

phrases.english: An animal whose legs were cut off,
from the knee joint and below, it is kosher;
from the knee joint and above, it is unfit;
and likewise if the convergence of the sinews was removed,
and Rav said about it: and likewise with a bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by pointing to a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a separate source (a משנה plus רב's comment) as the basis for the practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Checking the thigh seems to go against רב's ruling that a dislocated thigh is kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב himself said the משנה's rule about cut legs and the צומת הגידין applies to birds, so the checking is based on רב.

steps.title: רב seems to contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא points out that רב now appears to contradict himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: If so, there is a contradiction between one statement of רב and another statement of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא puts the two teachings of רב side by side and says they clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One teaching says a damaged thigh in a bird is fine (dislocated is כשרה). The other says thigh damage in a bird is like an animal's (פסולה). Both cannot seem to be right unless a difference is found.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between two statements of רב

phrases.english: And I said to him: If so,
Rav contradicts Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 3 into a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רב's two rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher, but also that the leg-cutting rule applies to birds. That looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: Maybe רב distinguishes between dislocated and cut
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה is silent, so רבי אבא himself suggests a way out: רב may treat a dislocated thigh differently from a cut one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. So I challenged him: But maybe רב makes a difference between a dislocated thigh and a cut one?
steps.whatsHappening: When רבי ירמיה has no answer, רבי אבא offers his own possible resolution of the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the two rulings deal with different cases. A bone that slipped out of place is not the same as a leg that was cut off. So רב could say the first is kosher and the second is not.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference for him

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up שמוטה (the bone slipped out of its socket) with חתוכה (the leg was actually cut). The whole answer depends on keeping these two apart.

phrases.english: He was silent, and I challenged him:
But perhaps Rav makes a difference
between a dislocated one and a cut one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא שָׁנֵי לֵיהּ לְרַב בֵּין שְׁמוּטָה לַחֲתוּכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: dislocated versus cut
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's two rulings may be about two different kinds of injury.

steps.title: רב said the distinction explicitly
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה confirms that the distinction is not just a guess, because רב said it outright: dislocated is כשרה, cut is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: And you are explaining רב's teaching on your own? רב said it explicitly: a dislocated thigh is kosher, a cut thigh is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה backs up the suggested distinction with an explicit statement from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between שמוטה and חתוכה is not something we have to work out ourselves; רב stated it directly. This removes the contradiction. Within רב's view, a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה, and checking is needed only for a cut or for the צומת הגידין.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this tradition of רב: in a bird, a dislocated thigh (שמוטה) is כשרה, and a cut thigh (חתוכה) is פסולה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לִי: וְאַתְּ מְפָרְשַׁתְּ שְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב?
phrases.english: And he said to me: And you are explaining Rav's teaching yourself?
phrases.notes: He means you don't need to work out the difference on your own, since רב already said it.

phrases.english: Rav said explicitly:
A dislocated one is kosher; a cut one is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the distinction suggested in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between שמוטה and חתוכה

steps.title: What tradition do you have?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רבי זירא what he himself received about this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you, what do you have in your hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The conversation turns around: now רבי זירא is asked to share his own tradition. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have only heard the tradition that a dislocated thigh is kosher. This question opens the door to a different report.

keyTerms.meaning: What is in your hand, meaning what tradition have you received?

phrases.english: And you, what is in your hand?
phrases.notes: He means what teaching have you received on this question.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי זירא's own tradition about a dislocated thigh in a bird

steps.title: A different tradition: a dislocated thigh makes a bird a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports, in the name of רב and also of רבי יוחנן, that a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה. And so said רבי יעקב בר אידי in the name of רבי יוחנן: a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the opposite tradition: a dislocated thigh does make a bird a טרפה, according to רב and also רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two conflicting reports of what רב held. One comes through רב הונא (כשרה), and one comes through רב חייא בר אשי (טרפה). רבי יוחנן also says טרפה, which adds weight to the strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
And so said, meaning a second authority agrees

steps.whatToRemember: There are two traditions in the name of רב. Through רב הונא, a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה. Through רב חייא בר אשי, it is טרפה, and רבי יוחנן agrees with the טרפה view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This conflict between reports of רב's view sets up the question of how to rule in practice on a dislocated thigh in a bird.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Thus said Rav Chiya bar Ashi in the name of Rav:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and so said Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A dislocated thigh in a bird is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a tradition opposite to step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה (רב through רב חייא בר אשי; רבי יוחנן through רבי יעקב בר אידי).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן would have deferred to the earlier assembly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי says that if רבי יוחנן had been where the earlier sages ruled the bird permitted, he would not have argued.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said: If רבי יוחנן had been in the place where the group of sages ruled that this bird is permitted, he would not have said a word against it.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after hearing that רבי יוחנן calls a dislocated thigh in a bird a טרפה, רבי יעקב בר אידי says רבי יוחנן would have backed down before the earlier sages who permitted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new voice on the permissive side. The claim is that the earlier sages were so great that רבי יוחנן would not have disputed their ruling. The next step will show who those sages were.

keyTerms.meaning: The group or assembly of sages
Stirred, moved; here it means to object or argue

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said:
If Rabbi Yoḥanan had been
in the place where the assembly ruled to permit it,
he would not have stirred.
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן would not have argued against their ruling at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי: אִילְמָלֵי הֲוָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי זירא's report that רבי יוחנן calls a dislocated bird thigh a טרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן would have deferred to the earlier sages who permitted the bird.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's salted hen that רבי permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports that רבי ruled a dislocated thigh in a bird כשרה. He kept the actual hen, salted, to teach his students.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said in the name of רבי: a dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher. רבי חנינא had a hen whose thigh became dislocated. He brought it to רבי, who permitted it. רבי חנינא salted it and used it to teach the הלכה to his students, saying: 'This is what רבי permitted to me, this is what רבי permitted to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous step by showing who permitted the bird: רבי himself, in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the support for the claim that great earlier sages permitted the bird. It was not only a teaching but a practical ruling on a real hen. רבי חנינא preserved that hen as living proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A thigh bone that slipped out of its socket (dislocated)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥanina said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: A dislocated thigh in a bird is kosher.
And Rabbi Ḥanina had a hen
whose thigh became dislocated,
and he brought it before Rabbi, and he permitted it to him,
and Rabbi Ḥanina salted it,
and he would teach the halacha with it to the students:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הִתִּיר לִי רַבִּי, זֶה הִתִּיר לִי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: This Rabbi permitted to me, this Rabbi permitted to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'assembly that permitted' mentioned in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That great earlier sages permitted a bird with a dislocated thigh.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's report of רבי's teaching and his ruling on a real hen.

steps.title: The halacha follows none of these opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the statements above that permit the bird, and introduces a story that will show the real halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not like any of these teachings. Rather, it is like the following:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces its ruling and sets up the next move. A conversation will follow that shows what the real halacha is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statements being rejected are the ones that permit the bird: רב הונא's report of רב (steps 1 and 6) and רבי's ruling (steps 9–10). The actual ruling, that a dislocated bird thigh is a טרפה, matches the strict tradition of step 8. The גמרא grounds it on the 'widespread הלכה' quoted in the conversation that follows.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not yet state the הלכה. The answer comes later, in רבי יהושע בן לוי's words (step 15): a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה.

phrases.english: But the halacha is not like any of these teachings,
rather, it is like this:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrules the permissive rulings of steps 1, 6, 9 and 10; the strict view of step 8 turns out to be the halacha.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The permissive statements (that a dislocated thigh in a bird is כשרה) are not the halacha; the following story shows the halacha is טרפה.

steps.title: How big a hole in the windpipe makes an animal a טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן נהוראי asks רבי יהושע בן לוי what size puncture in the windpipe makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן נהוראי asked רבי יהושע בן לוי: A hole in the windpipe — how big must it be?
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins with a simple question about the size of a windpipe puncture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question seems unrelated to the bird's thigh. But the discussion it starts will lead to the ruling on the thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: A puncture or hole in the windpipe

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁאֵל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Nehorai asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
A puncture of the windpipe — in what amount?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּשְׁאֵל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן נְהוֹרַאי אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that step 11 introduced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of a windpipe hole that makes an animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Up to the size of an איסר האיטלקי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers from a full משנה: the measure is the size of an איסר האיטלקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned a complete משנה about this: up to the size of an איסר האיטלקי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question by pointing to an explicit משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not his own opinion. It is a clear, accepted משנה, which makes it firm.

keyTerms.meaning: An Italian issar, a small coin used as a measure

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned a full Mishnah:
Up to the size of an Italian issar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measure for a windpipe hole is the size of an Italian issar, as stated in a משנה.

steps.title: But a ewe with a worse puncture survived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן נהוראי challenges him: a ewe with a punctured windpipe was patched with reed and lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But there was a ewe in our neighborhood whose windpipe was punctured. They made it a covering of reed, and it lived!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן נהוראי pushes back with a real case. An animal with this injury survived, so how can it be a טרפה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is an animal with an injury it cannot survive. If the ewe lived, it seems the injury is not deadly, which challenges the משנה's measure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא רָחֵל אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּשְׁכוּנָתֵנוּ
phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't there a ewe in our neighborhood
whose windpipe was punctured,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשׂוּ לָהּ קְרוּמִין שֶׁל קָנֶה וְחָיְתָה!
phrases.english: and they made it a covering of reed, and it lived!
phrases.notes: Here קנה means a reed plant, not the windpipe. Same word, different meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא רָחֵל אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּשְׁכוּנָתֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13 using a real-life case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a punctured windpipe (of that size) makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an animal with this injury survived, the injury is not deadly, so it should not be a טרפה.

steps.title: A hen with a dislocated thigh also 'lived'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rejects relying on such stories. A dislocated thigh in a bird is a widely accepted טרפה, yet רבי שמעון בן חלפתא's hen with one also survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And you rely on this? Isn't it a widely known הלכה in ישראל that a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה? And still, רבי שמעון בן חלפתא had a hen whose thigh was dislocated. They made it a tube of reed, and it lived!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that a survival story proves nothing. He gives another case where an animal survived even though everyone agrees it is a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If survival stories could overturn הלכה, they would also overturn the accepted rule that a dislocated bird thigh is a טרפה. Since nobody accepts that, the ewe story cannot overturn the windpipe rule either. Along the way, he states the הלכה our סוגיא needs: שמוטת ירך בעוף is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the הלכה promised in step 11 appears: a bird with a dislocated thigh is a טרפה, against רבי's permissive ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וְעַל דָּא אַתְּ סָמֵיךְ?
phrases.english: He said to him: And on this you rely?
But isn't it a widespread halacha in Israel:
a dislocated thigh in a bird is a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta had a hen
whose thigh was dislocated,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשׂוּ לָהּ שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל קָנֶה וְחָיְתָה!
phrases.english: and they made it a tube of reed, and it lived!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וְעַל דָּא אַתְּ סָמֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ewe proof of step 14 by giving a parallel case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using any survival story as proof that an injury is not a טרפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reasoning would overturn the accepted rule that a dislocated bird thigh is a טרפה.

steps.title: It only lived within twelve months
steps.stepSummary: Both survival stories are explained the same way: the animal was only seen alive within twelve months of the injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do you have to say about the hen? It was within twelve months. Here too, with the ewe, it was within twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains why the 'it lived' stories prove nothing. The animals were only seen alive for less than twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is defined as an animal that cannot live twelve months. Being alive for a while after the injury does not show it is healthy. The same answer that everyone must give for the hen also works for the ewe.
steps.whatToRemember: A wounded animal that survives for a while proves nothing; a טרפה can live up to twelve months. The הלכה: a dislocated thigh in a bird is a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
It was within twelve months;
phrases.notes: He means the hen was only seen alive during the first year, and a טרפה does not live past that.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי תּוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה.
phrases.english: here too, it was within twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reply to step 14 by explaining both survival stories.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Time limit: the survival was short of twelve months.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ewe lived, so a punctured windpipe is not a טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only lived within twelve months, which a טרפה can do; the rule stands.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא tested ideas; רבי יהודה's ruling on lost down
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא liked to test things and tried to disprove רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה held that a bird whose down was removed is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי שמעון בן חלפתא that he was a man who researched things. He would do things to disprove the view of רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה used to say: if the down of a bird was removed, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins, sparked by mentioning רבי שמעון בן חלפתא. It sets up his next experiment by first giving רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא introduces רבי שמעון בן חלפתא as someone who tested rulings in practice. The target is רבי יהודה's ruling that a bird stripped of its down is a טרפה. The next step tells what he did.

keyTerms.meaning: A researcher, someone who investigates and tests things
To remove from his heart; to disprove his view
Down, the soft feathers covering a bird's body

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta
that he was a researcher of matters,
and he would do something
to remove from the heart of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: He means: to show רבי יהודה's view was wrong.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Yehuda would say:
If the down was removed, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of רבי שמעון בן חלפתא's hen in step 15 to begin a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a bird whose down was removed is פסולה (a טרפה).

steps.title: The bald hen grew back better wings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא kept a hen without down warm in an oven, covered with a coppersmiths' apron, and it grew more feathers than before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא had a hen whose down was removed. He put it in an oven and covered it with a coppersmiths' apron, and it grew new wings with more feathers than the first ones.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the experiment itself. The hen recovered fully, as evidence against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said losing the down makes the bird a טרפה, meaning it cannot survive. רבי שמעון בן חלפתא showed that with warmth and care the bird recovered completely, and even grew back more than it had.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven; here used as a warm place

phrases.aramaic: וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta had a hen
whose down was removed,
and he placed it in an oven,
and he covered it with a coppersmiths' apron,
and the later wings grew
more than the first ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְנְגוֹלֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן חֲלַפְתָּא שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה נוֹצָה שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the experiment that step 17 set up against רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That a bird whose down was removed can recover, against רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא's hen, kept warm, which grew back more feathers than before.

steps.title: Maybe a טרפה can get healthier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the oven experiment. Perhaps רבי יהודה agrees that a טרפה can improve, so a healthy-looking bird would not disprove him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps רבי יהודה holds that a טרפה can actually get better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי שמעון בן חלפתא's experiment really disproved רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said a bird without its down is a טרפה. Maybe he would say that a טרפה can still look healthy, or even grow stronger for a while. If so, the hen doing well in the oven does not show that it was never a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: But perhaps Rabbi Yehuda holds
that a tereifa can improve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The oven experiment as a disproof of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a טרפה can improve, the hen's good health does not prove it was not a טרפה.

steps.title: It healed the very defect itself
steps.stepSummary: Even if a טרפה can improve, the hen grew back the very thing whose loss made it a טרפה. That does disprove רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if so, could it improve in the very thing that made it a טרפה, growing new wings with more feathers than the old ones?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the experiment. The hen did not just survive. It grew back the exact feathers that were missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: General improvement could still happen to a טרפה. But a טרפה cannot heal the defect that makes it a טרפה. Since the missing down grew back fully, losing the down was never a fatal defect.

keyTerms.meaning: The thing that makes it a טרפה

phrases.english: If so,
in the very thing that makes it a tereifa,
it grew later wings
more than the first ones?!

steps.whatToRemember: The experiment stands. Since the hen regrew the missing down, losing it is not a fatal defect.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between general improvement and healing the defect itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טרפה might improve, so the hen's health proves nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: A טרפה cannot heal the defect that makes it a טרפה. The regrown down shows it was never a טרפה.

steps.title: How did he earn the title 'researcher of matters'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what story earned רבי שמעון בן חלפתא the title 'researcher of matters.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story behind 'researcher of matters'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns away from the הלכה and asks about the title given to רבי שמעון בן חלפתא. It is setting up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 described him as someone who tested things. Now the גמרא wants to know which episode first gave him that reputation.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who researches and tests things

phrases.english: What is the story of 'researcher of matters'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 17, where he was called someone who liked to test things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side discussion about the title mentioned in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The episode that earned רבי שמעון בן חלפתא his title

steps.title: He set out to test a פסוק about ants
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says that רבי שמעון בן חלפתא read in משלי that ants have no ruler, and he decided to check whether this was true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: It is written, 'Go to the ant, lazy one, see her ways and be wise. She has no chief, officer or ruler, yet she prepares her bread in summer.' He said: I will go and see whether it is really true that they have no king.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא begins the answer. The title came from an experiment testing a פסוק about ants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק praises ants for working hard without any ruler. רבי שמעון בן חלפתא wanted to check the claim of 'no ruler' with his own eyes.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said: As it is written:
"Go to the ant, you lazy one,
see her ways and be wise,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהּ קָצִין שֹׁטֵר וּמֹשֵׁל,
phrases.english: which has no chief, officer or ruler,
yet prepares her bread in the summer."
He said: I will go and see

phrases.aramaic: אִי וַדַּאי הוּא דְּלֵית לְהוּ מַלְכָּא!
phrases.english: whether it is really true that they have no king!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He earned the title by testing the פסוק's claim that ants have no king

steps.title: The ant experiment
steps.stepSummary: He tricked the ants with shade from his cloak. They killed the ant that had misled them without any king's order, so he concluded they have no king.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went in the summer season of תמוז and spread his cloak over an ant hole. One ant came out, and he put a mark on it. It went in and told the others, 'Shade has fallen.' They came out, he lifted his cloak, and the sun beat down. They fell on that ant and killed it. He said: Learn from this that they have no king, because if they had one, wouldn't they need the king's permission?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן חלפתא carries out his experiment and draws his conclusion from how the ants acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ants avoid the hot sun, so the shade drew them out. When the shade vanished, they punished the ant that had 'lied' to them on the spot. A society with a king would need the king's order before putting someone to death, so he concluded the ants have no king.

phrases.english: He went in the season of Tammuz,
spread out his cloak
over an ant nest.
One of them came out,
and he placed a mark on it.
It went in and said to them: "Shade has fallen."
They came out,
he lifted his cloak,
and the sun beat down.
They fell upon it and killed it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לֵית לְהוּ מַלְכָּא,
phrases.english: He said: Learn from this that they have no king,
for if they had one,
would they not need the king's permission?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the test announced in step 22
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ants executed the misleading ant without any king's order

steps.title: The experiment proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא offers three other explanations for how the ants acted, so the experiment does not prove they have no king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: Maybe the king was with them? Or maybe they already had the king's permission? Or maybe it was a time between kings, as it is written: 'In those days there was no king in ישראל; each man did what was right in his own eyes'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא knocks down רבי שמעון בן חלפתא's conclusion by pointing out other ways to explain what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ants killing without a visible order does not rule out a king. The king could have been present, could have given permission in advance, or the throne could have been empty at that moment. The פסוק from שופטים shows that a people can have kings and still go through a time without one.

keyTerms.meaning: They were holding, meaning they already had
Between one king and the next

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps the king was with them?

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, הַרְמָנָא דְּמַלְכָּא הֲווֹ נְקִיטִי?
phrases.english: Or perhaps they already held the king's permission?

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי בֵּין מַלְכָּא לְמַלְכָּא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Or perhaps it was between one king and the next,
as it is written: "In those days there was no king in Israel;
each man did what was right in his own eyes"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי וְדִלְמָא מַלְכָּא הֲוָה בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion drawn in step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ant experiment as proof that ants have no king
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ants' behavior fits three other explanations: the king was present, permission was given in advance, or it was a time between kings.

steps.title: Rely on שלמה's word
steps.stepSummary: Since the experiment cannot prove anything, we rely on the trustworthiness of שלמה, the author of משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, rely on the trustworthiness of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story. We believe ants have no king because שלמה said so, not because of the experiment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The experiment was shown to be inconclusive. The claim still stands, but it rests on the authority of the פסוק in משלי that שלמה wrote.

phrases.english: Rather, rely on the trustworthiness of Solomon.
phrases.notes: שלמה wrote משלי, the book this פסוק comes from.

steps.whatToRemember: The ant experiment fails as a proof. We know ants have no king only because שלמה wrote it in משלי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes after the rejection in step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The claim that ants have no king rests on שלמה's authority, not on the experiment.

steps.title: Twelve months as the sign of a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that surviving twelve months is the sign that shows whether an animal is a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: The sign of a טריפה is twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא gives a test for an animal we are unsure about: if it lives twelve months, it is not a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is an animal with a fatal injury, so it is not expected to keep living. רב הונא sets twelve months as the amount of time that proves an animal is healthy. The next steps will test this number.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury or defect; it may not be eaten even if it is slaughtered properly

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
The sign of a tereifa is twelve months.
phrases.notes: He means: if a doubtful animal lives twelve months, it is not a טריפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the halacha after the story of the ants and makes a general rule of the twelve-month idea used in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that survives twelve months is shown not to be a טריפה.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists other signs, and none is twelve months
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives several different signs for a טריפה: not giving birth, getting weaker, or not surviving thirty days. None of them matches רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: The sign of a טריפה is any animal that does not give birth. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if it keeps getting better, it is surely kosher; if it keeps getting weaker, it is surely a טריפה. רבי says: The sign of a טריפה is thirty days. They said to him: But many animals live two or three years!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא that has three opinions about the sign of a טריפה. None of the opinions says twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses giving birth as the sign. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses the animal's health, and רבי uses thirty days. The חכמים reject thirty days because many טריפות live for years. Since no one in the ברייתא says twelve months, רב הונא seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps getting weaker and wasting away

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The sign of a tereifa is any animal that does not give birth.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If it keeps improving, it is certainly kosher;
if it keeps deteriorating, it is certainly a tereifa.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: סִימָן לִטְרֵפָה – שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: The sign of a tereifa is thirty days.
phrases.notes: He means: an animal that does not live thirty days was a טריפה.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא הַרְבֵּה מִתְקַיְּימוֹת שְׁתַּיִם שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים!
phrases.english: But many survive two or three years!
phrases.notes: They mean that many animals that are surely טריפות still live this long.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: סִימָן לִטְרֵפָה – כֹּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's twelve-month sign.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that twelve months is the sign of a טריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא records several opinions about the sign of a טריפה, and none of them is twelve months, so רב הונא's number seems to have no basis.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים, beginning with the skull ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב הונא follows one side of a dispute between תנאים. It starts to show this with a ברייתא about holes in the skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it is taught: And in the skull, when it has one long hole, or even many holes, they combine to the size of a drill hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that other תנאים do hold like רב הונא. It brings a ברייתא about a hole in the skull to set up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a hole in the skull the size of a drill hole makes an animal a טריפה, and several small holes add up to that size. The twelve-month idea does not appear yet. It comes out of the story and the reply in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
They join together, adding up to the required size
The size of a drill hole

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im,
as it is taught: And in the skull,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ נֶקֶב אֶחָד אָרוֹךְ,
phrases.english: when it has one long hole,
or even many holes,
they join together to make the size of a drill hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by saying the matter is a dispute between תנאים, and begins citing the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: רב הונא follows a תנא who is not in the challenging ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No תנא holds that twelve months is the sign of a טריפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another ברייתא shows a תנא whose view matches רב הונא.

steps.title: The man in עינבול who lived with a broken skull
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם tells of a man whose skull was missing a piece. They patched it with a gourd shell and he lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן המשולם said: There was an incident in עינבול with a man whose skull had a piece missing. They made him a patch from a gourd shell, and he lived.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בן המשולם tells a story to prove that a missing piece of skull does not have to be fatal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person survived with a missing piece of skull, then a skull injury would not make an animal a טריפה. This argues against the ברייתא in the step before.

keyTerms.meaning: Had a piece missing or broken away
A gourd, here its hard shell

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam said:
There was an incident in Inbul,
involving one whose skull was missing a piece,
and they made for him a patch out of a gourd shell,
and he lived.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּעִנְבּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that argues against the skull ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a missing piece of skull is not fatal
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the man in עינבול who survived with a gourd-shell patch

steps.title: He lived only through the summer and died in the winter
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rejects the proof. The man lived only during the summer and died as soon as winter came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said to him: Is that a proof? It was summer, and as soon as the winter days came upon him, he died right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rejects the story as a proof. The man did not truly survive, because he died once winter came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, living a few months proves nothing. An injury is shown to be survivable only if the animal lives through both summer and winter, a full year. This is the תנא whose view matches רב הונא's twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (meaning, it proves nothing)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that surviving is proven only by living through summer and winter. This is the source for רב הונא's twelve months.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 27. רב הונא's twelve-month sign follows the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said to him:
Is there proof from there?
It was summer,
and once the winter days came upon him,
he died immediately.
phrases.notes: The point is that real survival means lasting through summer and winter, a full year, just like רב הונא's twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי בן המשולם's proof, and in doing so shows the source for רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the man in עינבול
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He lived only through the summer and died in the winter, so he never really survived.

steps.title: The הלכה: a טריפה can give birth and even improve
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rules that giving birth and improving in health do not prove an animal is not a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב says: The הלכה is that a טריפה can give birth and can get healthier.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the practical ruling. Giving birth and getting healthier are not signs that an animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rejects two signs from the ברייתא in step 27: the first opinion's sign of giving birth, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's sign of improving health. A טריפה can do both, so neither one can show that the animal is kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, an animal giving birth or getting healthier does not prove it is not a טריפה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, הֲלָכָה:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov says: The halakha is:
A tereifa can give birth and improve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the signs listed in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Giving birth and improving health are not reliable signs that an animal is kosher.

steps.title: אמימר begins a statement about eggs from a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר starts a new statement about eggs laid by a bird that is a טריפה. The statement continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר says: These eggs of a טריפה...
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next topic. אמימר starts talking about eggs from a טריפה bird, and his ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the ruling just given that a טריפה can give birth. If a טריפה bird can lay eggs, we need to know how to treat those eggs. אמימר's answer appears in the continuation.

phrases.english: Ameimar says:
With regard to these eggs of a tereifa,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the ruling that a טריפה can give birth, and turns to eggs from a טריפה bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not finished here; אמימר's ruling about eggs from a טריפה continues in the next part of the text.
